title: Two maps of the same health system disagree — and not at random
subtitle: OpenStreetMap recovers 17.1% of Philippine and 11.8% of Bangladeshi clinical-tier facilities in official registries.
finding: OpenStreetMap captures 17.1% of the Philippine clinical-tier national health-facility registry and 11.8% of the Bangladeshi registry. Both pilots sit well below a 30% fit-for-planning threshold, with a consistent rural–urban gradient.
finding_short: PHL 17.1% and BGD 11.8% clinical-tier OSM match rates.
limits: Registry–map disagreement, not corrected facility locations or service access.
Does not measure quality of care, utilization, or population coverage.
Poverty-context rows multiply a gap proxy by incidence only where SAE joined—not affected population.
key_messages: Both PHL and BGD show material OSM under-count of official clinical facilities.
Worst ADM1 match rates fall to about 6% in BARMM and Barisal.
The pattern is a map-observability finding, not a health-system performance ranking.

sections.title: When two maps disagree
sections.body: Access maps often treat OpenStreetMap facility points as if they were the service network. Official registries tell a different story. The research object is source disagreement, not a finished access index.

sections.title: Cross-country headline
sections.body: In the Philippines, OSM holds 17.1% of clinical-tier NHFR facilities (range 6.5% BARMM to 63.5% NCR). In Bangladesh, OSM holds 11.8% of DGHS facilities (range 6.2% Barisal to 20.1% Dhaka). Both patterns show a rural–urban gradient.

sections.title: How match is defined
sections.body: Clinical-tier active facilities in each official registry are compared to OSM health features under a documented spatial and class filter. ±50% sensitivity is complete for both pilots with no critical failures under the committed gates.

sections.title: Poverty context is a join, not a welfare claim
sections.body: A Philippines ADM3 poverty-context table joins official SAE incidence to the existing gap proxy. It is not affected population, demand, or welfare loss.

sections.title: Maturity
sections.body: Publication-ready package pending owner-only Zenodo DOI. Internal and external red-team reviews are closed under §18 AI-first attestation.

workbench_rows.label: Philippines
workbench_rows.note: Strong rural–urban gradient; map-observability object retained.

workbench_rows.label: Bangladesh
workbench_rows.note: Independent second pilot supports the same pattern.

non_claim: This measures registry–map disagreement and map observability. It does not correct locations, rank health systems, or estimate access, utilization, or welfare.
